Name: Wormhole Greatwyrm
Information:
**Wormhole Dragons**

These deep-space dragons are a blight to ships that happen to encounter them, and a shadow looming in every debris belt and asteroid moving through exolunar space. They are predatory by nature, seeking anything that sparks their curiosity and destroying anything that gets between them and it. They are highly intelligent when it comes to reasoning and planning, but their isolation leaves them selfish and with a childish mentality, so much so that they don’t consider the effect they have on other creatures.

**Flippant Motivations.** A wormhole dragon is motivated entirely by a focus on breaking from its usual boring patterns: their life in exolunar space rarely holds surprises, and sometimes it can take decades for anything to come through their part of space. As a result, they seek out excitement and try to get the most out of toying with lesser creatures that catch their attention. They can be won over by those who promise them amusement or by people who strike them as fascinating, but they usually get bored with their arrangements and muses quickly. They may even betray allies of “lesser standing” in their boredom, hoping the resulting turmoil will be fun to navigate.

**Cosmic Predators.** Wormhole dragons are cunning hunters who lurk among rocks and meteors to patiently wait for prey to come to them. Utilizing their ability to warp and shift around space, they use hit-and-run tactics to injure their prey then retreat and plan their next move. They are more agile than most dragons, and exploit that for the purposes of overcoming the dangers of exolunar space.

Luckily, most wormhole dragons see the hunt as mere fun. They often keep their sustenance in their lairs and have set hunting grounds they warp between, so their “opportunistic” hunts are more often than not just a ploy to pass time. They may attack a spacefaring vessel until the excitement passes or it poses any moderate threat, then will warp away and leave it in disrepair.

**Planetary Tourists.** Occasionally, a wormhole dragon will choose to visit a populated planet and live for some time as a resident there. They will assume the form of a local creature and spend a human lifetime exploring and “window shopping” in their society. These stints of exploration are a hobby to them, which they gleefully indulge in to pass time. While ingratiated with a society, they will slowly find people and things they desire and lure them to a situation where they can warp them back to their lair, keeping them as possessions, servants, or concubines.

A wormhole dragon’s exit from such a “vacation” will usually involve revealing itself in the process of stealing something of great importance: a high ranking public servant, a landmark, an entire building or treasury, etc. To the dragon, taking people, places, and things doesn’t cause lasting damage to the world they come from; on the contrary, they see it as enriching their personal world contained in their lair, and see the acquisition of servants as inviting them into a paradise.

**Egocentric Tells.** A common reason for such a dragon being caught in a disguise is due to their consistent inability to recognize the cultures they insert themselves into as their own. Even if they live 100 years on a planet, they will still speak as though they were visiting and use language that separates “their world” from the one they’re inhabiting. Though not obvious at a glance, this behavior can raise suspicions.

**A Wormhole Dragon’s Lair**

These cosmic dragons build their lairs in caves dug out from large dead planetoids or space debris, sometimes inhabiting asteroids. They are experts at outfitting their lairs with amenities they need: they will use their wormhole abilities to hunt for sources of water, food or objects it desires, and create a wormhole that pulls the target or a substantial portion of it back to their lair. They may land on a planet to create such a disturbance in a lake to drain it into its own lair, for example. To this end, they tend to compartmentalize their lairs to have large chambers to store these resources independently.

Once it has spent time within it, the dragon’s warping eventually causes their lair to form an atmosphere where oxygen is produced and life can exist. This atmosphere is supernaturally tied to the dragon, and if the dragon dies its layer will vanish within 1 day. For particularly ancient wormhole dragons, these lairs can even be city-sized, allowing a following or ecosystem to thrive in this pocket of life.

A wormhole dragon will usually take the deepest chamber of its lair as its nest, where it surrounds itself with various curiosities from places it’s visited. Given its warping abilities, it will sometimes steal entire monuments, temples, etc. to bring there, making its lair a puzzling fusion of chunks of locations it has taken for its own amusement. They are cunning enough to also steal civilians and powerful individuals, warping them to its home and leveraging their isolation against them to force them to act as servants. By these means, a wormhole dragon can force the hands of any beast capable of reason, though it risks losing their aid if a way to escape ever presents itself.

**Quote**

“Humanoid forms come and go as needed, but the form of humans and astral elves are my favorites. They have a charming efficiency and elegance to them, and can pop up anywhere across the galaxy. As useful as they are appealing.”

traits.name: Scourge of the Universe (Mythic Awakening)
traits.description: If the dragon is reduced to 0 hit points or outright killed, it instead resets to 450 hit points, recharges its breath weapons, regains all uses of its Legendary Reaction, and for 1 hour it can use its Mythic Actions. A party who defeats the dragon after it uses its Mythic Awakening gains an additional 120,000 XP (240,000 XP total).

traits.name: Sympathetic Warp
traits.description: When the dragon uses its teleport speed, any creature mounting it or who is being grappled by/grappling the dragon directly teleports along with it. This does not end these grapples.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The dragon makes one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +17 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 20 (2d10 + 9) piercing damage plus 17 (3d10) force damage.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +17 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 20 (2d10 + 9) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Tail
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +17 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 31 (4d10 + 9) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Devastation Wave (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: The dragon creates an inverted gravity well that projects out from it in a 300-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 25 Strength saving throw, taking 88 (16d10) force damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. Each creature who fails by 5 points or more is also pushed 100 feet back from the dragon and knocked prone. Creatures pushed back who collide with a surface that stops them early take 1d10 bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet they stop short.

actions.name: Wormhole (Recharge 6)
actions.description: The dragon produces the effects of the teleport spell. When it does it leaves a black hole-like spherical disturbance in space where it vanished, which fills a sphere centered on the dragon with a 50-foot-radius. There is a 20% chance that the disturbance may collapse at the start of each of the dragon’s turns, sealing it. While it is present, any creature who ends their turn in the disturbance or enters it for the first time on their turn must succeed on a DC 20 Charisma saving throw or be teleported to the nearest unoccupied space in the same location the dragon teleported to.

bonus_actions.name: Change Shape
bonus_actions.description: The dragon transforms into its true form or into any creature that is Medium, Small or Tiny, while retaining its statistics (other than its size), though if it is Tiny it cannot use its Multiattack. This transformation ends if the greatwyrm is reduced to 0 hit points.

options.name: Attack
options.description: The greatwyrm makes one Claw or Tail attack.

options.name: Shimmer Strike (Costs 2 Actions)
options.description: The dragon teleports into an unoccupied space it can see within 120 feet and makes one Claw attack.

mythic_actions.description: The dragon may use the following actions as Legendary Actions for 1 hour after using their Mythic Awakening.

options.name: Bite
options.description: The dragon makes one Bite attack.

options.name: Dimensional Shunt (Costs 2 Actions)
options.description: The dragon chooses one of the following: three creatures it can see within 120 feet, or all creatures in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on a point within 120 feet. Each target is caught in a wormhole and must make a DC 25 Charisma saving throw. On a failure they are shunted to an interstitial demiplane as though under the effects of the banishment spell for 1 minute. The dragon must concentrate on this effect as though it was a spell.

lair_actions.initiative: On initiative count 20 (losing ties), the wormhole dragon may take a Lair Action to cause one of the following effects; the wormhole dragon cannot use the same effect twice in a row.

options.name: Force Trap
options.description: Three creatures the dragon chooses who it can see within 120 feet have a cage of gravitational force form around them. They must succeed a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or become Sluggish for 1 minute. A creature made Sluggish this way takes 1d10 force damage at the start of each of their turns, and repeats the saving throw at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect on a success. This effect ends early if the dragon takes another Lair Action.

options.name: Gravity Center
options.description: The dragon chooses one direction in its lair which must correspond to a surface with a flat plane. The lair becomes a low-gravity environment, with the chosen plane being the new “down” orientation. This effect ends if the dragon takes another Lair Action.

options.name: Worm Network
options.description: The dragon chooses four points it can see within 120 feet. Spherical wormholes open in those spaces, forcing each creature within 20 feet of each to make a DC 15 Strength saving throw or be pulled into it. Creatures pulled into these wormholes take 2d10 force damage, and are then spat out in an unoccupied space the dragon chooses within 15 feet of one of the wormholes. Which wormhole serves as an exit for each creature is determined randomly and individually.

legendary_reactions.source_conversion_note: Converted from Legendary Resistance (3/Day) per standing formatting rule.
